descriptionChirho: To take someone aside privately, often for correction or instruction (Mt 16:22; Mk 8:32; Acts 18:26).
To receive or welcome a person into fellowship, community, or hospitality (Rom 14:1,3; 15:7; Phlm 1:17; Acts 28:2).
To take something for oneself, especially food, or to recruit or enlist people for a purpose (Acts 17:5; 27:33-36).
